## New functions

A tuning of the `bbmle::mle2()` function:

```{r}
mle3 <- function(...) {
  bbmle::mle2(..., method = "Nelder-Mead", control = list(maxit = 1e4))
}
```

A tuning of the `bbmle::coef()` function:

```{r}
coef2 <- function(x) exp(bbmle::coef(x))
```

A tuning of the `bbmle::confint()` function:

```{r}
confint2 <- function(x) exp(bbmle::confint(x))
```

A function that excludes values from a vector `x` by their names `e`:

```{r}
exclude <- function(x, e) x[grep(e, names(x), value = TRUE, invert = TRUE)]
```



## Serial dilution data

A function that formats the serial dilution data:

```{r}
format_serial_dilutions <- function(x) {
  x |> mutate(across(c(CFU1, CFU2, CFU3),
                     ~ .x / (`Inoculum volume (Ml)` * `Countable Dilution`))) |> 
    select(`OD values`,  CFU1,  CFU2,  CFU3) |> 
    pivot_longer(-`OD values`) |> 
    select(-name) |> 
    rename(OD = `OD values`, concentration = value)
}
```

Loading the serial dilution data:

```{r}
SD_M9 <- serial_dilutions |> 
  read_excel2("SD M9") |> 
  format_serial_dilutions()

SD_M9Fe <- paste("SD M9+Fe", 1:3) |> 
  map_dfr(~ read_excel2(serial_dilutions, .x)) |> 
  format_serial_dilutions()
```

A function that formats the data of growing populations:

```{r}
format_growing_populations <- function(x) {
  x |>
    mutate(across(CFU, ~ .x / (`Inoculum volume (Ml)` * `Countable Dilution`))) |> 
    select(OD_600,  CFU) |> 
    rename(OD = OD_600, concentration = CFU)
}
```

Loading the growing populations data:

```{r}
GP_M9 <- serial_dilutions |> 
  read_excel2("GP M9") |> 
  format_growing_populations()

GP_M9Fe <- serial_dilutions |> 
  read_excel2("GP M9+Fe") |> 
  format_growing_populations()
```

Combining the serial dilution and the growing population data for the `M9` and the
`Me+Fe` media:

```{r}
(dilution_data <- list(list(SD_M9,   GP_M9),
                      list(SD_M9Fe, GP_M9Fe)) |> 
  map(~ bind_rows(set_names(.x, c("SD", "GP")), .id = "method")) |> 
  set_names(c("M9", "M9+Fe")) |> 
  bind_rows(.id = "medium"))
```

Plotting the dilution data:

```{r}
#| label: fig-serial_dilution
#| fig-cap: "Relationship between optical density and bacterial concentration as estimated by CFU counts in two different experimental setups: at regular points in time along a natural growth of the culture (population growth) or by serial dilutions of an initial concentration (serial dilutions). The vertical lines show threshold values of the optical density above which optical density values are not correlated any more with bacterial concentrations."

dilution_data |> 
  mutate(across(concentration, ~ .x * 1e-6),
         pch = (method == "SD") + 1,
         col = cols[medium]) |> 
  slice_sample(prop = 1) |> 
  with(plot_od(concentration, OD, pch = pch, col = col,
               xlab = "concentration (CFU/nL)"))

thresholds <- set_names(c(.48, .75), media)
abline(h = thresholds, col = cols)

legend("bottomright", ncol = 2, bty = "n",
       legend = c(media, "population growth", "serial dilutions"),
       col = c(cols, "black", "black"), pch = c(15, 15, 1, 2))
```

It shows that above some threshold values of OD, the OD values should not be used to
quantify any growth.



## Culture data

Loading the data and expressing time in minutes:

```{r}
(od_data <- culture_data |>
  read_excel2() |> 
  group_by(Sample, Medium) |> 
  mutate(replicate = row_number()) |>
  ungroup() |> 
  pivot_longer(- c(Sample, Medium, replicate), names_to = "time", values_to = "OD") |> 
  mutate(across(time, ~ .x |>
                  str_remove(" *h$") |> 
                  as.numeric() |> 
                  multiply_by(60) |> 
                  round() |> 
                  as.integer())))
```

Looking at the levels:

```{r}
(unique_levels <- od_data |> 
  select(-OD) |> 
  map(~ sort(unique(.x))))
```

Checking the regularity of time measurements:

```{r}
unique(diff(unique_levels$time))
```

The number of combinations:

```{r}
unique_levels |> 
  map_int(length) |> 
  reduce(`*`)
```

Number of replicates per combination:

```{r}
(nb_rep <- od_data |> 
  group_by(Sample, Medium, time) |> 
  tally())
```

Checking that we have all the combinations:

```{r}
nrow(nb_rep)
```

Looking at the number of replicates per combination:

```{r}
nb_rep |> 
  pull(n) |> 
  unique()
```

A function that plots the data:

```{r}
plot_data <- function(x, ...) {
  x |>
    mutate(across(time, ~ divide_by(.x, 60))) |> 
    slice_sample(prop = 1) |> 
    with(plot_od(time, OD, xlab = "time (hours)", col = cols_alpha[Medium], ...))
  legend2("topleft")
}
```

Plotting the OD values:

```{r plot_OD_values}
#| label: fig-culture
#| fig-cap: "Cultures growth shown as optical densities as a function of time. Horizontal lines show threhsolds above which optical densities cannot be converted into bacterial concentrations anymore. That clearly rules out the exploitation of the some potential K phase of a logistic growth." 

plot_data(od_data)
thresholds |>
  (\(x) abline(h = x, col = cols[names(x)]))()
```

Discarding the data points with OD values below the thresholds:

```{r}
#| label: fig-serial_dilution2
#| fig-cap: "Same as @fig-serial_dilution where the data have been filtered to show only the values of optical densities that correlates with bacterial densisty. This is the data that will be used to estimate the exponential growth rates in the section that follows."

od_data2 <- filter_out(od_data, OD > thresholds[Medium])
plot_data(od_data2)
```



## Exponential rates

A function that computes the maximal (i.e. exponential) growth rate in a way that it is
robust to any latency phase before the exponential growth actually starts:

```{r}
compute_r <- function(x, k = 20, by = 1) {
  x |> 
    mutate(across(OD, log)) |> 
    gam(OD ~ s(time, k = k), data = _, method = "REML") |> 
    predict(list(time = seq(min(x$time), max(x$time), by))) |> 
    diff() |> 
    max()
}
```

Computing the exponential growth rates for each replicate:

```{r}
r_values <- od_data2 |> 
  group_by(Sample, Medium, replicate) |> 
  group_modify(~ tibble(r = compute_r(.x))) |>
  ungroup()
```

Plotting the growth rates of replicates arranged by strain and culture medium:

```{r}
#| label: fig-growth_rates
#| fig-cap: "Estimated maximal (i.e. exponential) growth rates arranged by strain and culture media."

labels <- unique(r_values$Sample)
ats <- labels |>
  (\(x) set_names(seq_along(x), x))()

r_values |> 
  mutate(across(Sample, ~ jitter(ats[.x])),
         col = cols[Medium],
         col_alpha = cols_alpha[Medium]) |> 
  with({
    plot(Sample, r, col = col, xaxt = "n",
         xlab = "strains", ylab = "exponential growth rate (/minute)")
    points(Sample, r, col = col_alpha, pch = 19)
  })

axis(1, ats, labels)
legend2("topright")
```



### Verifications

```{r}
predictions <- function(data, model, by = 1) {
  t <- data$time
  tibble(xs = seq(min(t), max(t), by)) |> 
    mutate(pred = predict(model, list(time = xs)))
}

# predictions(models$data[[1]], models$model[[1]])
```

```{r}
find_max_growth <- function(df) {
  df |> 
    mutate(across(pred, ~ c(NA, diff(.x))),
           across(xs, ~ c(NA, head(.x, -1) + diff(.x) / 2))) |> 
    slice(-1) |> 
    filter(pred == max(pred)) |> 
    unlist() |> 
    setNames(c("infl_t", "growth_r"))
}

#predictions(models$data[[1]], models$model[[1]]) |> 
#  find_max_growth()
```

```{r}
plot_data_model <- function(data, predictions, time, col) {
  with(data, plot(time, OD, pch = 19, col = col,
                  xlab = "time (minutes)", ylab = "log(OD)"))
  with(predictions, lines(xs, pred, lwd = 2, col = col))
  abline(v = time, col = 2, lwd = 2)
}
```

```{r eval = FALSE}
inflexions <- od_data2 |> 
  mutate(across(OD, log)) |> 
  nest(.by = c(Sample, Medium, replicate)) |> 
  mutate(model = map(data, ~ gam(OD ~ s(time, k = 20), data = .x, method = "REML"))) |> 
  mutate(predictions = map2(data, model, ~ predictions(.x, .y)),
         out         = map(predictions, ~ find_max_growth(.x))) |> 
  unnest_wider(out)
```

```{r eval = FALSE}
inflexions |> 
  select(data, predictions, time, Medium) |> 
  pwalk(~ plot_data_model(..1, ..2, ..3, cols[..4]))
```



## Growth models

### Utility functions

A function that fits a growth model `m` by maximum-likelihood to data `x` using a
probability distribution `f`:
  
```{r}
calibrate <- function(x, m, f, start = NULL, k = 1, ...) {
  if (is.null(start)) start <- m$ini_val(x, k)
  out <- mle3(m$mLL_factory(x, f), start, ...)
  out@data <- list(data = x, model = m$model, distribution = f)
  out
}
```

A function that retrieves the probability distribution used from a fitted model `x`:
  
```{r}
get_distr <- function(x) attr(x@data$distribution, "name")
```

A function that retrieves the growth model used from a fitted model `x`:
  
```{r}
get_model <- function(x) attr(x@data$model, "name")
```

A function that retrieves the data from a fitted model `x`:
  
```{r}
get_data <- function(x) x@data$data
```

A function that generates predictions in times `t` from a fitted model `x` and with
confidence interval `ci`:
  
```{r}
t_vals <- seq(0, 15 * 60, le = 512)

predictions2 <- function(x, t = t_vals, ci = .95) {
  params <- coef2(x)
  f <- attr(x@data$distribution, "q")
  q <- function(mu, lower = FALSE) f((1 - ci) / 2, mu, params["k"], lower.tail = lower)
  tibble(time = t,
         fit  = do.call(x@data$model, c(t = list(t), exclude(params, "k"))),
         lwr  = q(fit, TRUE),
         upr  = q(fit))
}
```

A function that plots the model's prediction:

```{r}
plot_predictions <- function(x, col = col_M9, alpha = .3, add = FALSE, ...) {
  with(x, {
    t <- time / 60
    if (! add) plot_od(t, fit, type = "n", ...)
    polygon(c(t, rev(t)), c(lwr, rev(upr)), border = NA, col = adjustcolor(col, alpha))
    lines(t, fit, col = col, lwd = 2)
  })
}
```

A function that adds data points:

```{r}
add_data <- function(x, col = col3) {
  with(get_data(x), points(time / 60, OD, col = col, pch = 19))
}
```

Let's combine them:
  
```{r}
plot_fit <- function(pred, fit, ylim = NULL, col_data = 2, col_model = 4,
                     alpha = .3, ...) {
  if (is.null(ylim)) {
    OD <- get_data(fit)$OD
    ylim <- c(min(c(pred$lwr, OD)), max(c(pred$upr, OD)))
  }
  plot_predictions(pred, col_model, alpha, ylim = ylim, ...)
  add_data(fit, col = col_data)
}
```

A wrapper:
  
```{r}
plot_fit_and_data <- function(fit, ...) {
  fit |> 
    predictions2() |> 
    plot_fit(fit, ...)
}
```



### Probability distributions

A function that builds probability distribution functions that packages everything we
need:
  
```{r}
distribution <- function(name, d, q) {
  attr(d, "q") <- q
  attr(d, "name") <- name
  d
}
```

Definining the normal probability distribution function:
  
```{r}
normal <- distribution("norm", function(x, mu, k) dnorm(x, mu, k, log = TRUE), 
                       function(x, mu, k, ...) qnorm(x, mu, k, ...))
```

Defining the log-normal probability distribution function:
  
```{r}
log_normal <- distribution("lnorm",
                           function(x, mu, k) dlnorm(x, log(mu) - k^2 / 2, k, log = TRUE), 
                           function(x, mu, k, ...) qlnorm(x, log(mu) - k^2 / 2, k, ...))
```

Defining the gamma probability distribution function:
  
```{r}
gammad <- distribution("gamma", function(x, mu, k) dgamma(x, k, k / mu, log = TRUE), 
                       function(x, mu, k, ...) qgamma(x, k, k / mu, ...))
```


### Growth models

Defining the exponential growth model:
  
```{r}
exponential_growth <- function(t, N0, r) N0 * exp(r * t)

attr(exponential_growth, "name") <- "exponential"

exponential <- list(
  model = exponential_growth,
  
  mLL_factory = function(x, f) {
    function(N0, r, k) {
      -sum(f(x$OD, exponential_growth(x$time, exp(N0), exp(r)), exp(k)))
    }
  },
  
  ini_val = function(df, k = 1) {
    p <- setNames(c(coef(lm(log(OD) ~ time, df)), k), c("N0", "r", "k"))
    p[-1] <- log(p[-1])
    as.list(p)
  }
)
```

Defining the logistic growth model:
  
```{r}
logistic_growth <- function(t, K, r, t0) K / (1 + exp(-(t - t0) * r))

attr(logistic_growth, "name") <- "logistic"

#ini_val_logistic = function(df, k = 1) {
#  time <- df$time
#  OD <- df$OD
#  K <- max(OD)
#  halfK <- K / 2 - min(OD) / 2                    # (second term could be optional)
#  evaluate <- function(x) approx(time, OD, x)$y
#  distance <- function(x) abs(evaluate(x) - halfK)
#  t0 <- optimize(distance, range(time))$minimum
#  r <- df |> 
#    filter(time < t0) |> 
#    mutate(across(OD, log)) |> 
#    lm(OD ~ time, data = _) |> 
#    coef() |> 
#    extract(2) |> 
#    unname()
#  tibble(K = K, r = r, t0 = t0, k = k)
#}

logistic <- list(
  model = logistic_growth,
  
  mLL_factory = function(x, f) {
    function(K, r, t0, k) {
      - sum(f(x$OD, logistic_growth(x$time, exp(K), exp(r), exp(t0)), exp(k)))
    }
  },
  
#  ini_val = function(df, k = 1) {
#    df |> 
#      group_by(replicate) |> 
#      group_modify(~ ini_val_logistic(.x, k)) |> 
#      ungroup() |> 
#      select(-starts_with("replicate")) |> 
#      colMeans() |> 
#      log() |> 
#      as.list()
#  }
  
  ini_val = function(df, k = 1) {
    time <- df$time
    OD <- df$OD
    K <- max(OD)
    halfK <- K / 2 - min(OD) / 2                    # (second term could be optional)
    evaluate <- function(x) approx(time, OD, x)$y
    distance <- function(x) abs(evaluate(x) - halfK)
    t0 <- optimize(distance, range(time))$minimum
    r <- df |> 
      filter(time < t0) |> 
      mutate(across(OD, log)) |> 
      lm(OD ~ time, data = _) |> 
      coef() |> 
      extract(2) |> 
      unname()
    map(list(K = K, r = r, t0 = t0, k = k), log)
  }
)
```



### Dev

Mean negative log-likelihood:

```{r}
MNLL <- function(x) x@details$value / nrow(x@data$data)
```

```{r}
stationary_end <- function(data, model, distribution, maxt) {
  1:maxt |> 
    map(~ data |> 
          slice(-(1:.x)) |> 
          safely(calibrate)(model, distribution)) |>
    map_dbl(~ ifelse(is.null(.x$result), 1e6, MNLL(.x$result))) |> 
    which.min()
}

#stationary_end(aaa$data[[1]], logistic, normal, 18)
```

              distr = list(normal, log_normal, gammad)) |>
    mutate(end_station = map2_dbl(model, distr,
                                  ~ stationary_end(data, .x, .y, infl_index)),
           fit = pmap(list(end_station, model, distr),
                      ~ calibrate(data[-(1:..1), ], ..2, ..3)))
